title: "Appendix D. Cumulative impacts of mining and wind power development on reindeer: calving-site selection data and analysis"
author: ""
#author: Léonie Duris, Bernardo B. Niebuhr, Erik Cronvall, Moudud Alam, Per Sandström, Anna Skarin
abstract: |
  Here we present a detailed description of the data, methods, and results related to the calving-site selection analysis for reindeer under the presence of the mine and the wind turbines in the Malå reindeer herding district in Sweden. The calving site is the location where the female gives birth and spends time with the calf outside the herd to create an attachment bond. Taking into account different zone of influence (ZOI) radii for mining and different scales for the topographic position index, we fitted a total of 21 candidate models for calving-site selection and compared them through model selection procedures. We report: (i) the method to assess calving period and site identification; (ii) the description of the statistical models of cumulative impacts; (iii) the model selection table comparing the structure and likelihood of the different models; (iv) the analysis of calving site selection and forage quality.

# Text D1: Statistical modeling of cumulative impact analysis

As in the landscape-scale habitat selection analysis, we used a habitat selection function setup. However, considering only individuals within 2 km of the wind turbines during calving to assess the effect of wind power drastically reduced the number of observations, preventing the use of the habitat selection function for that purpose. The habitat selection function was therefore used only to assess the mine's zone of influence.

Ten random available but unused sites were generated within the estimated calving area for each of the truly used calving sites (R package `amt`, function `random points()`). We determined the calving area by calculating the minimum convex polygon around all the used calving sites. To ensure consideration of the entire calving area, we extended the estimated area to half the mean net square displacement of individuals that calved at the border of the minimum convex polygon.

The overall model structure we fitted was:

```{r}
base_formula <- case_ ~ 
  # habitat selection
  scale(dem) + I(scale(dem)^2) + scale(slope) + cos_aspect + 
  log(power_lines_dist+1) + log(priv_road_dist+1) + log(public_road_dist+1) + 
  log(trails_dist+1) + 
  # mining habitat selection
  scale(mining_Krist_nearestXXX) +
  # wind habitat selection
  landcover + phase*log(wind_turbines_dist + 1) +
  # tpi habitat selection
  tpi_scale_TTT
```

where the terms are:

-   `case_`: our response variable (0/1);
-   `dem`: elevation, we include a linear and a quadratic term;
-   `slope`: slope;
-   `cos_aspect`: cosine of the aspect;
-   `tpi_scale_TTT`: topographic position index (TPI) as a continuous variable and computed at a certain scale;
-   `phase`: wind power plants development phase, with 3 categories: before construction, during construction, operation;
-   `wf_name`: name of the wind power plant closest to each point, with four categories, added as a fixed effect to control for differential effects close to the Åmliden wind park, which lies along a large fenced area;
-   `landcover`: land cover, with 5 categories: deciduous forest, coniferous forest, open areas, mires, and anthropogenic areas;
-   `log(public_road_dist+1)`, `log(priv_road_dist+1)`, `log(trails_dist+1)`,   `log(power_lines_dist+1)`,`log(wind_turbines_dist_comb + 1)`: logarithm of the distance to the nearest infrastructure for public roads, private roads, trails, houses, power lines and wind turbines;
-   `mining_Krist_nearestXXX`: ZOI (exponential decay distance) of the mine, computed considering a certain ZOI radius;

The terms `XXX`, and `TTT` in the model structure above represent scales or variables that varied across models fitted. To evaluate the most likely ZOI for the mine and at which scale the TPI most affected reindeer habitat selection, we replaced these variables in the model structure above using each possible combination of ZOI radii for the mine and different scales for the TPI. Models were compared through Akaike information criterion (AIC), as described in the main text. The scales included were:

-   Mining (`XXX`): 100 m, 250 m, 500 m, 1 km, 2.5 km, 5 km, 10 km.
-   TPI (`TTT`): 150 m, 250 m, 510 m.

All fixed terms are shared across models, and only the mine ZOI and TPI scale varied. Consequently, all models had the same number of parameters. This combination of possible variables resulted in a total of 21 models tested and compared.

# Table D1: Model selection table in calving sites

```{r aic_calving, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| label: aic_calving
#| fig-cap: "Table D1. Table of model selection for the calving site selection model. Columns are zone of influence (ZOI) radius for mining, scale for the topographic position index (TPI), log-likelihood and AIC of the model, dAIC of each model in relation to the most parsimonious model, and the formula with each model's structure. The best-ranked model includes the variables mining ZOI = 10km and TPI = 250m; models with TPI = 510m and 150m have low difference (<2) in AIC in comparison to the best ranked model."

aic_calving <- readr::read_csv("results/CSV/calving_sites_rsf_calving_AIC_table_complete_20261023.csv")

aic_calving |> 
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("log", mining)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dAIC = aic - min(aic),
                rel_likelihood = exp(-0.5 * dAIC),
                akaike_weights = rel_likelihood / sum(rel_likelihood),
                akaike_weights_text = ifelse(akaike_weights < 0.0001, "< 0.0001", round(akaike_weights, digits = 4)),
                cumulative_akaike_weights = round(cumsum(akaike_weights), digits = 4),
                logLik = round(loglikelihood, 1),
                dAIC = round(dAIC - dAIC[1], digits = 2),
                aic = round(aic, digits = 2),
                tpi = sub("tpi_s", "", tpi),
                tpi = sub("_end", "", tpi)) |> 
  dplyr::relocate(definition, .after = last_col()) |> 
  dplyr::relocate(logLik, .after = tpi) |> 
  dplyr::select(-c(lc, wind, rel_likelihood, loglikelihood, akaike_weights)) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Mining ZOI radius` = 1,
                TPI = tpi,
                AIC = aic,
                `Akaike weights` = akaike_weights_text,
                `Cumulative Akaike weights` = cumulative_akaike_weights,
                formula = definition) |> 
  # DT::datatable()
  make_table(col_widths = c("1.5cm", "0.75cm", "1cm", "1cm", "1.25cm", "1.15cm", "1.15cm", "6.5cm"))
```

# Table D2: Final model results

Here we show the coefficients for the best-ranked model. The second and third-ranked models had similar support from the
data and only differed in the scale of the TPI considered; all other coefficients were similar.

```{r final_model, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| label: coef_general
#| fig-cap: "Table D2. Coefficient estimates of the most parsimonious generalized linear model testing the effect of infrastructures on reindeer calving site selection from the Malå reindeer herding community between 2008 and 2018. The table includes the estimates, the standard error (std.error) and the p-values (p)."

# read calving
coef_calving <- read.csv("results/CSV/rsf_calving_AIC_table_log2.csv", sep = ",", dec = ".")

coef_calving |> 
  dplyr::mutate(significant = as.factor(if_else(p.value < 0.05, 1, 0)),
                p = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", round(p.value, 3)),
                select = case_when(
                  (estimate > 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate < 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "avoidance/negative",
                  (estimate < 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate > 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "selection/positive",
                  TRUE ~ "no effect"
                )) |> 
  dplyr::select(-c(statistic, significant, p.value)) |> 
  # DT::datatable()
  make_table()
```

Colors in the plots represent the distribution of all individuals, only those within 2km of the wind turbines during the calving period, and only those that were always more than 2km away.
